newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda spending 130 mln shillings on coffee wilt.
newsitem.headline: Uganda spending 130 mln shillings on coffee wilt.

text.p: Uganda will spend 130 million shillings ($123,000) in a fight against tracheomycosis, which has affected at least 11 coffee growing districts, the state Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said on Wednesday.
UCDA Managing Director Tress Buchanayandi told Reuters the cash would go to research and replacement of destroyed trees.
"We have put a small fund of 130 million Uganda shillings to carry out replacement of infected materials and do research in breeding resistance," he said in an interview.

He said the outbreak of tracheomycosis, or coffee wilt disease, was not yet alarming and would not affect the total coffee production this year, estimated by economic development minister Richard Kaijuka at 4.4 million kg.
"We are going to contain it (the wilt disease). The outbreak is not yet out of hand," Buchanayandi said.
The UCDA planned to train extension staff to identify symptoms typical of the disease and carry out disease surveillance. The research could continue for up to three or four years.
Tracheomycosis destroys a tree's vascular system leaving a scar on the tree stem after which the tree dies. It does not affect berries.
